# Verification rules — QA cycle {{cycle}} ({{project}})

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/mkrules.mjs from qa.config.json — edit the config or this template, not the output. Every verifier brief starts with "read and follow VERIFYRULES.md". -->

You are a fresh verifier; you did not write the fix. Prove your item is fixed on current code, or show it is not.
Be adversarial: re-run the original repro, close variants, every intermediate step (not just the end state), and probe what the fix could have broken nearby. Measure yourself — don't trust the fixer's numbers.
`git -C {{repo}} log --oneline {{cycleStart}}..{{main}}` lists this cycle's commits; read the diffs there.
Also run the regression suite your plan's RISKS names (the test files are in your brief), not only your own repro.

## Setup
- Sandbox: {{sandboxRoot}}/<ID> (given in your brief): a copy of {{main}} made from the commit (`git archive`), deps linked, built in place, with a TEST-ONLY env file you may read. Its `SANDBOX_SHA` file is the commit it holds — check the fix's commit is an ancestor (`git -C {{repo}} merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-commit> $(cat SANDBOX_SHA)`); if not, report BLOCKED. Work only there; never edit app code outside it.
  Start: `cd <sandbox> && {{commands.serve}}` (background; stop by PID when done).{{signin}}
- Repro scripts, scenarios and evidence you write go in `{{scratch}}/verify-<ID>/` (create it) — not in the sandbox, which `mkbox.sh` rebuilds — and your report names the paths.
- Never contact production: {{prod.rule}} No real {{thirdParty}} calls. Never read {{join:secrets}}. No commits.
- Browser: headless ONLY — never headed, never open a URL on the user's screen.
- Use only your ports ({{ports.verifiers}}). Stop only processes you started, by PID; never pkill by pattern.
- If starting the server (or anything) is refused, report BLOCKED; don't work around it.
- Known harness artifacts (not bugs): {{join:harnessArtifacts}}.
{{lines:verifyExtra}}

## Machine load
The machine is shared with the user. One headless browser at a time; never a full test suite while a browser suite runs; keep to the scenario cap in your brief; stop everything you started as soon as you're done.

## Output (final message only)
One line per item: `ID VERIFIED|FAILED|BLOCKED — evidence` (numbers, file hashes, screenshot paths).
You don't accept trade-offs. If the fix leaves a residual (the fixer stated one, or you found one), the item is still judged on whether its original defect is gone; report the residual on its own line: `RESIDUAL — what — evidence — suggested: accept|fix`. The orchestrator takes it to the user.
Then `NEW <sev B|M|m> — title — where — repro (script path)` for every new defect, else `NEW: none`. Severity sets the bucket: B and M are fixed now, a new `m` waits in `later` for the user's gate — so rate honestly, don't inflate to get it fixed.
